utterances.text: Yes. I pulled it down myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know or was it your view that it contributed to the tension in Mostar at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, certainly it didn't assist in good relations with the different groupings there. It's -- it worried me when I saw it, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I want to ask you just a few questions about what developed there in Mostar - you talked about it in your witness statement - which was a joint commission. Do you know -- or did you know at the time that ECMM had tried to build or -- or make these joint commissions in other areas throughout the former Yugoslavia or was this an idea that they came up with as a way to deal with the situation in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, the joint principle of the joint commission, there's nothing new in it. It's been used around the world in different theatres. It's an idea of just bringing the different groupings together and try and lower tension when a problem arises, so preventing some escalation in -- in force. The idea of the joint commission in Mostar was, to the best of my knowledge, was - it was Mr. De Castella's idea originally. I can't be a hundred per cent sure about it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel and witness please pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is the ambassador you're referring to who was in Split?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes, mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And it was suggested that you should try to build a joint commission in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And so then can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, the idea was that we would get again the key leaders and where -- where a problem existed in that region and I quote one example in Jablanica where there were defensive positions being built by Muslims, that you would go there, identify the problem, and ask the relevant parties to resolve the problem thereby allowing the tension in the area -- to reduce the tension in the area. It sounds very simplistic and it is, I suppose, simplistic. When used properly as a tool as we subsequently see for example in Gornji Vakuf, it's quite effective.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall who were the representatives of the joint commission from the respective parties in November of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: As I say, the joint commission really did not get off the ground in Mostar. The commitment wasn't there towards it. Originally the plan was that Mr. Petkovic and Pasalic would be members of the joint commission, but as I say it really -- it never really got going.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say the commitment wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Just -- commitment from -- from -- it appeared from the HVO at the time wasn't into the joint commission procedure because maybe they didn't see that it was an effective tool.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did the ABiH on the Muslim side, did they appear to support the notion of a joint commission?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: They were more supportive of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So as a result then the joint commission never really took hold, is that --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. No, it really didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then was the idea then ultimately abandoned or --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. And time moved on and tension increased and other problems then arose. You know. As I've tried to explain to people about Mostar at that particular time we were, as I said, limited assets, limited resources working 16, 17 hours a day. We had a huge amount on our plate, huge amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During this period again November - December 1992, based on your dealings with the various parties and the situation, did you have any observations about whether the Muslims or the ABiH for their part were wanting to make -- wanting to do things that would contribute to reducing the tension?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: At that particular time it was my opinion based on what I had witnessed that the Muslims were more inclined to support ideas that would assist in reducing the tension in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And based on your observations, can you give us an idea of the relative strengths militarily as between the two sides at this time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, again when you say relative strengths, I mean I cannot give you brigades assets, military assets, but I can say that it appeared to me as a military person that the HVO were a structured organisation with a -- with a command and control -- with a command and control system that appeared to work, and they had definite military assets, artillery and armoured vehicles. The Armija on the other side, I was never quite convinced about their command and control capability and I did not see their military assets. I could not compare their artillery or military vehicles to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, was the municipality of Stolac within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: When I -- when I said you there that we were so busy working 16 to 18 hours a day, and as I pointed out we had extremely limited resources, both in equipment and personnel, Stolac was an area that took up a lot of my time and my team in Siroki Brijeg's time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you have one particular experience in Stolac related to the hospital at Kostana?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. One of my teams, in fact the team from Siroki Brijeg, went on a fact-finding mission -- mission to Stolac, and they -- they had an HVO liaison officer with them, and they went through the town basically carrying out a reconnaissance of the town, people, damage to property, significant events. As they passed the hospital -- the hospital in Stolac, they noticed that there were bed linen on a line at the back of the hospital, so they turned round and went in. They had been informed that the hospital was empty. And they went in and did, as I say, a reconnaissance of the hospital where they found a significant number of people, I think in the region of 120, in quite deplorable conditions housed up in this building. They then came back to Siroki Brijeg and reported that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the time just to set the context, if you will, Stolac was in the area of an active front line with the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. Yes. In fact, to get into Stolac from -- from our side required going through a number of check-points and then avoiding the threat and the actuality of Serb artillery fire or rapid fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The check-points were manned by --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this hospital in this area of Stolac, which -- did it fall within the Serb zone or the HVO zone?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The hospital was a sanctuary for people who really had nowhere to go. The -- the oldest person in the hospitals was in their 80s and the youngest was a child. Whether it was in the Serb -- or sorry, whether it was in the Croat or the Muslim side, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You saw that the HVO accompanied your -- your people down there on the first time --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- on that first day. And then did you subsequently go down there on the next day?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: My team asked me to accompany them on the next day and see for myself, because the picture they painted was extremely bleak and I just wanted to see it myself and we went down. And the picture they had painted was precisely what I saw on the ground. I saw people living in the most terrible situation. I saw every tree on the front of the hospital had bullet marks in it. Most of the tops of the trees had been blown away. There were actually no -- very few windows in the building. There was some sort of a local contraption for collecting rainwater as a source of water. There was no medicines. It was -- it was -- it was a sad sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you then raise this issue, the issue of the people at the hospital, with people on the HVO side?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Again I refer to key leader engagement. This was a significant event. All significant events would be briefed to the relevant authorities to see what action could be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if you raised this with Mr. Bozic in particular?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Again, I repeat it. It was raised with key -- with the key leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you attempt subsequently to go back down to this hospital and were you able to gain access?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Once our interest in the hospital became known, quite a number of restrictions were placed on -- attempted restrictions were placed on our movement to the location. However, these were eventually lifted and we got access to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were the -- were you -- well, what was your objective in respect of these people? Did you try -- want to get them out of there, evacuated, or aid down to them, or what was then the objective?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I have very -- I'm a simple soldier and I have simple priorities in life and one of them is called preservation of life. I applied it to my own people -- my own people who worked for me in Bosnia, and I apply it to everybody, irrespective of colour or whatever. These people were living in deplorable conditions. This could not be allowed to continue. And as in Posusje, I would take whatever action I required to improve their livelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Right. Do you know if the situation or conditions down there improved at any time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I visited the parish priest in Medjugorje because I was aware that at that time quite a significant amount of humanitarian aid was being sent to Medjugorje from the Republic of Ireland, my own country. Ireland, as you're aware, is a Roman Catholic country, and people in Ireland have great affinity for Medjugorje and for the Croat population there. I asked, as politely as I could, that some of this humanitarian aid which was forwarded with the -- with the best of intent from Irish people be given to me and I could transfer it to the hospital in Medjugorje -- in Stolac. Fortunately -- unfortunately, this request wasn't acceded to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commandant, when you were at the hospital, do you remember the exact date? Was it November or December? Or perhaps you don't remember at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately as I've said time has moved on, 15 years, I actually not a date on it and I'm surprised in a way because it was a defining moment for me when I went to visit that hospital and it has stayed with me ever since I visited that site. So I apologise, I actually can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We might be able to narrow down the time frame. Let me direct you to Exhibit 10289 which I believe is at the back of the binder. 10289. So you said you didn't receive support of Father Slavko in Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I think it would be fair to say that I received no support.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And did you receive support from anyone else or anyone on the HVO side on this?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: When I say I received no support, no support.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- which then brings me to this Exhibit 10289. Do you recognise this, sir?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's a newspaper article --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- written by a gentleman named Fisk?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Robert Fisk, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, how this article then figures into the story of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Again, I repeat what I say. In every theatre I've served in, no matter what part of the world, I always -- when I see something wrong, I've tried by whatever means to improve -- to improve the situation. Stolac had a profound effect on me, and you probably hear in my voice it still has today. I was aware that Robert Fisk, who is a renowned reporter for the London Independent, was working in the Kiseljak/Sarajevo area. So I decided to go up and talk to him about the possibility of coming down to the Mostar area and covering a number of stories, particularly the Stolac story, to try and alleviate the suffering of these people. Fisk agreed to my offer and came down and he wrote a -- a very emotional and detailed article on the plight of these people in Stolac. The article we're looking at here is in fact is an article that was subsequently put into the Irish Times but the original article was on the London Independent.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You've had a chance to review this article. Does it accurately in your view describe the conditions that were at the hospital at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I want to make it clear that when I invited Fisk to come down, what I said to him is as follows: He would be taken to a number of areas. He would not be briefed on anything by me or my people. He would see what he see and he would write what he -- what he would subsequently write, and what you see there is his -- his report on what he witnessed. It's -- I really haven't got any -- any criticism of it. I think it's a true and accurate reflection of what went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall having a conversation with Mr. Stojic about the publication of this article?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The -- the article caused me -- caused me some problems when it was -- when it -- obviously not the Irish Times version but the Independent version, and there was annoyance within the HVO at the highlighting of this in the world international press, and this displeasure was passed on to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall who passed that displeasure on to you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. -- Mr. Stojic. I can't be a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, I want to shift gears a little bit and ask you now a series of questions about a different location, that of Gornji Vakuf, farther to the north. Upon your arrival in Western Herzegovina, were those areas - Prozor, Gornji Vakuf - were those areas that presented themselves as areas meriting your attention?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: As I said to you originally, my plan was always to move north of Mostar, to move into these particular areas, and again -- again, repeating what I said at the very start of this, the ECMM presence was there to assist all sides as much as possible, identify problems and try and solve or assist in some way. So when I say my intent was to move north, it was, absolutely to move north. And I was also aware that there were problems in the Prozor-Gornji Vakuf area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you go up towards Prozor and Gornji Vakuf during the middle --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- of November 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I did. I took -- we moved to Prozor-Gornji Vakuf, again I think second week of November, again I can't be a hundred per cent sure of the date unfortunately, but it was around that particular time. Again, why we were there: To carry out a reconnaissance of the area, to ascertain what was happening on the ground, to meet, where possible, key leaders again, and again draw a picture of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, we're going to talk about Gornji Vakuf later in the month of January in a little bit but focusing on this, was this your first trip up to Gornji Vakuf then?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did you get there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Excuse me. We drove north of Mostar, up to Jablanica and up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Then after Jablanica it would have been what town or city would --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Oh, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You'd go through Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, sorry. I thought you meant -- no, we arrived in Prozor and then to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At that time, then, on this first visit, were there any check-points or obstacles you needed to pass through?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. There were -- there were a number of check-points, but having said that we had no problem getting through those check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall what you saw as you passed through Prozor then on your way toward Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. We saw quite an amount of damage to properties in the -- in Prozor itself. I also identified on the hills around Prozor some artillery pieces. Obviously not firing, just positioned pointing toward the Prozor area and that was it. We moved on then to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at that time did you know which -- those artillery pieces which army or militia those belonged to?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I take an educated guess, but to answer your question, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. So then you left Prozor and headed up toward Gornji Vakuf. Can you tell us then what you saw when you reached that area?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: We went up and we got up to the Makljen Ridge overlooking. We tried to find the vantage point or key ground that we could just see Gornji Vakuf from, just to see what was going on. We saw a certain amount of shelling into the Gornji Vakuf area which kind of supported some information that I had received. Black smoke on the ground, you know, after some artillery shells fired into it, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I should have asked you what was it that caused you to Gornji Vakuf in the first place?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause between question and answer for the sake of interpreters, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. I apologise. The -- I had been approached in -- at a particular time by somebody who said that the ECMM should go to Prozor, Gornji Vakuf area to monitor what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, as you left Prozor and headed up toward Gornji Vakuf, did you then pass through additional check-points?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know which party controlled that area that this Makljen ridge you referred to?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The -- the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we've got a map that I'd like to use with the witness when we talk about these areas. I think it will be useful during a later stage of the direct, and what I propose to do is -- is ask the witness to use one with the ELMO and then we have copies for the Trial Chamber and counsel as well. It's a little bit tricky because the text is pretty small on this but we'll do our best. Were the other ones distributed yet? Did ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What I'm going to do, Witness, and maybe at this point I could ask the usher to distribute the other maps, and while that's happening, Witness, maybe the best thing is if you just take the map over to the desk there and if you can find this feature that you've just mentioned, which is the Makljen feature. Maybe if you could take a pen and just put a circle around that on the map, then everyone else would at least have an idea of what you're -- if you have a pen.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Okay. Obviously -- we obviously approached Gornji Vakuf on this road here. Here we have Gornji Vakuf -- Gornji Vakuf here, and the idea was to find high ground around here that we could look into Gornji Vakuf to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Now, again I cannot remember specifically the location that we stopped, but it was vantage point and it was high ground to allow us to see in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Looking at the map, and you might have to look closely, but are you able to find indicated on there the Makljen Ridge or feature a little bit above Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you see it there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why don't you place a circle around that.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Is this on --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my question -- the first question on this, Witness, is this appears to me to be rather some distance from Gornji Vakuf itself, and so --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That's the point I'm making. We -- when I -- when you refer to the Makljen Ridge, we actually moved forward to high ground where we could actually see Gornji Vakuf down below us. I mean, it's -- it was just high ground we had located.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So you could have been above or below --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, we were absolutely above that. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you give a rough indication of where you were?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll accept that. Are you able to give some indication how close you actually got to the town of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: All we -- all I can say is that we were on high ground. We could see Gornji Vakuf in the distance and we could ascertain that there was fire into Gornji Vakuf and that was all I wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what type of fire?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It appeared to be -- it appeared to be artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since we can see the elevations on the map, et cetera, it would be important for the witness to say precisely where it was possible for him to see Gornji Vakuf, from which vantage point it was possible for him to see Gornji Vakuf. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has been asked what was his position, and he says at this point he can't remember exactly where he was. I think that we have to take the answer as it's been given. I asked the witness at line 2 of page 60, can you give a rough indication of where you were. That was my intended question. And the witness says, I can't remember. And then all he can say is that they were on high ground. "We could see Gornji Vakuf in the distance." So the witness is not in a position to indicate it on a map as I've asked him to do. Shall I continue, Mr. President? I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commandant, when you have a look at the map and you are unable to tell us where you were exactly, but between Makljen and Gornji Vakuf, well, it's more than 5 kilometres between Makljen and Gornji Vakuf, that's for sure. So from the vantage point you were at did you have a view of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I stated I had a view of a section of Gornji Vakuf. It wasn't a total view of the town of Gornji Vakuf. It was just a section. Unfortunately, again, I regret that I can't actually remember precisely where I was, but it's 15 years ago, but I do have the view of Gornji Vakuf in my mind now as I speak to you, and I could see it below me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. A minor technical question: Did you have binoculars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Another question which might help a little. Do you remember whether the place where you were had been accessible by car or whether you walked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We parked our vehicle and we walked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, now --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should ask for an IC number for that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour the document just marked shall be assigned Exhibit number IC 693.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So, Witness, what we've just been talking about is your initial trip up toward Gornji Vakuf through Prozor in November. I think it was -- is that correct? Was it in November?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now then, I'd had like now to talk about events involving Gornji Vakuf then that occurred during the month of January 1993, and were you involved and aware of events in respect of Gornji Vakuf then in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was aware that the -- the situation in Gornji Vakuf had deteriorated to the extent that we were being informed that there was armed conflict in Gornji Vakuf and in some of the surrounding towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I asked you earlier about information or briefings from UNPROFOR, and did you obtain information from UNPROFOR about the situation that was taking place in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was given which is -- I was given quite a detailed briefing by UNPROFOR on the disposition of forces in the particular area, both HVO and Armija forces in the area, and the determination of the UNPROFOR troops in Gornji Vakuf was that there was quite a serious conflict about to break out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the information you got related to the positions of HVO artillery and troops at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: He spoke about HVO troops massing on Makljen as you have pointed it out there. The roads being closed off north of Gornji Vakuf and the town itself being isolated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what was the position, the location of the British Battalion, the UNPROFOR, in respect of Gornji Vakuf and the HVO there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR troops in -- based in Gornji Vakuf, the Cheshire Regiment, had attempted to organise a local cease-fire between the different parties, but unfortunately that failed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So they were engaged in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, then on the 18th of January, 1993, do you recall if then you personally went up to Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: On the 18th of January, having been briefed, as I've said, on the situation in Gornji Vakuf, I decided to go up to Gornji Vakuf myself so I would be in a position to carry out a reconnaissance, gain as much information as I could and bring it back with me back to RC Split, because the situation appeared to warrant the intervention at quite a senior level of EC personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at this period of time who was the chief or the head of the regional centre in Split?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mr. Bousseau.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what country was he from?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: French.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So he was your direct superior by this time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: He was my direct superior. He also had a very keen interest and knowledge of the area and spent quite a significant amount of time in that area. He became extremely involved in what was subsequently to happen in Gornji Vakuf. In fact, when I refer to key leader engagements, he was the key leader in this -- in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did he accompany you to Gornji Vakuf on the 18th of January?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. On the 18th of January, I went -- I went up with a monitor, an interpreter and a driver, and because the situation had deteriorated so much we had to leave our vehicle a good distance from Gornji Vakuf, and we met the UNPROFOR personnel with their Warrior armoured cars who escorted us into the UNPROFOR headquarters in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber then the situation as you found it at the UNPROFOR headquarters --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- at Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: -- The drive from Gornji Vakuf from where we left our armoured vehicle was quite interesting. There was a significant number of artillery round falling, we could hear from the blast. Quite extensive firing, so much so that my interpreter became extremely upset and -- very, very upset and had quite a difficulty placating her when we eventually got to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you know at the time or did you subsequently learn where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, having served in Lebanon for so many years, I was -- I'm -- I was aware of what they know -- what they say is incoming and outgoing. This was incoming into the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you able to give us a rough idea how close you were to the town -- or perhaps I should ask you what was the location of the UNPROFOR headquarters then?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR headquarters was actually in Gornji Vakuf. It was -- from what I remember, it was an old factory that they had just taken over and they were using it as accommodation, workshops for the vehicles and they had a number of rooms allocated for -- for -- as offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is it a location you think you could indicate for us on this map?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, I -- not at all, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was it in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. No, it was in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if it was to the south --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- or to the north of the main road?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, once you arrived at the UNPROFOR headquarters, were you able to -- to see more about the shelling where it was coming from or where it was landing, the locations of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: There was a serious conflict, a serious -- serious number of rounds landing in Gornji Vakuf, and as I say, I have quite a bit experience in the Middle East and I was even taken aback by the severity of the -- of the incoming. Outgoing there was small-arms fire, but I did not hear artillery or tank fire outgoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you learn at that time or subsequently which party or side was conducting the shelling and also the small-arms fire? I mean, can you give us the relative positions or --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, it was -- it was the view of UNPROFOR operations in Gornji Vakuf that the incoming was from the HVO and the outgoing small-arms was from the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to get -- do you know roughly the -- when you say shelling, I want to try to be a little more specific on the nature of the weaponry that's being used. I mean, are we talking about rocket launchers, mortars, tanks?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: We're talking about artillery rounds. I do remember some rockets, but definitely artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the areas in Gornji Vakuf where the shelling was landing, did these appear to be -- well, can you describe the location? Was it the town, houses, structures, buildings? What was --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was quite surprised that the fall of shot in a lot of cases were into domestic dwellings. Quite a number of -- of -- quite a number of rounds actually fell not too far away from where we were in -- in UNPROFOR headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the artillery weaponry that you're describing, can you give us some sense of where that was located --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- In reference -- in relation to the --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- town?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, that is the 18th of January. The following day do you recall what -- what took place? Well, let me just ask you this: On the 18th did you -- did you stay then --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- spend the night --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- at the UNPROFOR headquarters or did you return to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: We returned back to our coordination centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me direct your attention then, Witness, to Exhibit P 1215, which is in the binder. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just turning to the last page, the third page. Does that appear to be the signature of the head of your regional centre, Mr. Bousseau?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And this report makes reference to a meeting. Well, it says: "Persons met: Jadranko Prlic, Mr. Arif Pasalic, Mr. Petkovic." You see that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall where the meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I have a feeling it took place in Mr. Prlic's office, but I couldn't guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us - and you're free to read this through if you'd like before you answer more questions - but I would like to ask you just in general the purpose of the meeting, points discussed at it.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: May I read it? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, take your time.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't object to the witness refreshing his recollection. I take it now that he's testifying from the document. In other words, he's just going to read the document and then regurgitate whatever's in the document; it's not from his independent memory of any meeting if he did attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr.--

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A distinction needs to be made. Is he going to be vouching for the gentleman who generated this or is he testifying from his independent memory? Which of the two because it goes to weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not going to ask the witness to regurgitate. I'm going to conduct my direct examination and counsel can cross-examination if he has questions that go to weight?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman was in the Office of the Prosecution over the weekend. Obviously they showed him some documents. Now he's asking the witness to read and then he's going to comment on it. Is he refreshing his memory? Is this something that he knows about? What is it? If he's just going to read back what's in the document, then it's not testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, you must have shown him this document to him this weekend. I assume so at least. So the document he read at the time since it was signed by his superior, well, do you want to ask him questions about what one can find in the document or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to ask him to read the document for us, Mr. President, but I think that he's talking about a meeting he had with Mr. Prlic, Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Pasalic. I am going to ask the witness what he remembers about the meeting. I think -- I'm not accustomed to objections in advance of questions so I'm not sure what to say. I asked him to read the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue to put your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And at the meeting I want to ask you if you recall: As between Mr. Prlic and Mr. Petkovic, who appeared, based on what you observed, to be in a higher position or a position of greater authority in terms of decision-making?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, the witness said that he recalled the meeting. He didn't say that he took part in it. Was he present at the meeting? This question has not yet been answered, and it would be interesting, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I thought that I'd asked the question, Mr. -- Or Judge, but I will ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, were you present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes, mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this was you and Mr. Bousseau?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Prlic, Petkovic, Pasalic. Others, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I can't remember if there were others. Interpreter, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So then coming back to my question, in this meeting, based on what you observed as between Mr. Prlic and General Petkovic who appeared to be in a greater position of decision-making and authority?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Could you ask the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Based on what you observed at this meeting, who appeared, if you recall, as between Prlic and Petkovic, did one appear to be in a position of greater authority in relation to the other?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to you and to my colleague, but I believe that it is my duty to draw your attention to the fact that this document shows that we're not dealing with one meeting. Item 1 says "Persons met" and about General Petkovic, my client, it says that he came without having previously announced himself to our meeting with Mr. Pasalic. So one could draw the conclusion that the meeting that Mr. Prlic is one meeting, the one with Mr. Pasalic another one and my client came unannounced to a meeting with Mr. Pasalic. So before we try to discuss this any further, perhaps we should clarify this. I think this would be useful for everyone. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Stringer. Ask the witness where the meeting was held, who was around the table, who chaired the meeting, and gradually we'll see matters more clearly if he has any recollection. If not, you'll just move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I thought I asked you already. I'll ask you again if I didn't. Are you able to recall the location where the meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: As I said when you asked me previously, I felt it was in Mr. Prlic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And this is the location where you had been to meet with him on other occasions as well?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: On the Rondo roundabout, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On the Rondo?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Roundabout.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you recall again - I think it's been asked - who was present at the meeting, and if it was chaired by any individual, who chaired the meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, again, due to it's so long ago, my only recollection of the meeting is the people listed there and the people I've mentioned. And that's the reason I was reading over this again just to clear up my own mind what was actually -- what was actually said. The people I've listed are the people I remember. If there were other people at it I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Based on that answer, Mr. President, I'd ask that the witness be instructed not -- or the Prosecutor be instructed not to ask any more questions with respect to this particular document since he doesn't recall the meeting. He doesn't recall the substance. They can bring in the gentleman that generated this document to go into details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think that's the witness's testimony at all. Though it doesn't surprise me that counsel would like to pass over this document and this meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have no problems with the document itself. I suggest that my learned friend look at the answer. He says, "Unfortunately again due to so long ago my only recollection of the meeting is the people listed there and the people I've mentioned." And that's why I'm reading it over again." He read it over the weekend, obviously it didn't refresh his memory. Mr. Stringer allowed him to read it again, it still hasn't refreshed his memory. He has no memory, other than the people. So, what I'm saying, Mr. President, is he doesn't have an independent recollection. The document, obviously, is going to be coming in. But unless he can demonstrate that he has an independent recollection of the meeting, he cannot comment about the substance of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me suggest that counsel is putting words into the mouth of the witness which is unfair and which have not been said by the witness. I asked the witness, who was at the meeting. That's what he was talking about in terms of his recollection, who was present. I'll ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of the people whom you remember were present?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Prlic, Petkovic, Pasalic, Bousseau, Lane and an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not in dispute. What is in dispute is the substance and that's what I am trying to say and I think Mr. Stringer is deliberately misleading the Trial Chamber. The record speaks for itself; he indicated that he has no recollection, other than the people who attended the meeting. We can agree to that. There is no dispute. The document will be coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put the question to the witness myself. Sir, you said that there was a meeting. Fine. As far as you can remember -- well, can you remember the people present at the meeting, the purpose of the meeting, and the questions or issues that were dealt with at the meeting? As far as you can remember. Don't look at the document. Look at me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, Your Honour, the purpose of the meeting was discuss to clearly the situation in Gornji Vakuf. It was an attempt to -- to terminate the hostility in Gornji Vakuf. My reason for being at that meeting was I was being tasked clearly by Mr. Bousseau to go to Gornji Vakuf with whatever was agreed at that meeting and see could it be implemented in Gornji Vakuf. Of that I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In the meeting referred to in the document and as far as you can remember, was it Mr. Prlic who took the floor first or did someone else present the situation? Did Mr. Pasalic take the floor? Did you take the floor? Do you have any recollection of this or not? If not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I think I've said already, Your Honour, my recollection is the reason for the meeting was to terminate the hostilities in Gornji Vakuf. My purpose at being at the meeting was to take whatever was agreed at that meeting to Gornji Vakuf and implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not answering the question, Mr. President, and I'm glad that you asked the question because a previous question was who seemed to have more authority. Then it had to be pointed out that Mr. Petkovic actually came into the meeting later on. So in fairness, the witness doesn't have a recollection, but I don't think -- but he needs to answer the question directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if counsel says enough times that the witness doesn't remember, that doesn't make it the truth. This witness is saying he remembers the meeting. He remembers the people there. Maybe not all of them, but he remembers the one that mattered, including counsel's client. Now, I'm going to stay with this as long as it takes and I will sit out every intervention were my learned friend in order to fully flesh out what this meeting's about based on the witnesses recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I hope I can assist. It appears that perhaps we are belabouring over a needless point. As I understand it, my learned friend Mr. Karnavas is not disputing the alleged meeting itself, and of course my learned friend from the Prosecution is perfectly entitled to put questions. I think the confusion, with respect, appears to have arisen because rather than, first of all, ascertaining the independent recollection of the witness, we have muddied the waters to some extent with this document. Your Honour, of course a document can be used for a number of purposes, but absent a clear recollection it can either note -- be used to -- well, for two types. Either evidence of past recollection recorded or present recollection revived. So it's not clear if the witness's memory is being revived from looking at this document so that he therefore vividly recollects the incident that he had previously forgotten, understandably, the details 15 years ago, or if in fact he can merely state that this is a document which appears to come from -- from the sender of the document and it was made contemporaneously at the time. Your Honour, I don't know if that assists matters, but it appears the dispute is not about the meeting; it's simply about the details. Can the witness recollect it independently of this document. Of course, you have the document yourselves and it's a matter of weight in conjunction with the rest of the evidence you hear. I don't know if that can help put us back on track, but I certain hope so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You have said everything. You have said it all. What counts is to learn, as Mr. Khan says, whether the witness has a recollection of the meeting. If not, then we can look at the document. We have to disconnect the witness from the document. First ask him questions about his recollection. If he doesn't remember, then we can refresh his memory by saying on page X or paragraph Y it is stated such-and-such. That is how you should proceed, Mr. Stringer. Otherwise, there are objections and everybody is wasting time. We need to know who did what, what was the purpose of the meeting. He has told us. What was said? Who did what? He either remembers or not. If he doesn't remember, we have to rely on the document, which I think is already admitted, I don't know, but it seems to me that I've already seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you're hearing all of this and maybe it's just more efficient for me to ask you to tell us what do you remember about the meeting as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, I think I've already said the purpose of the meeting was to try and solve the problem of Gornji Vakuf with the key leaders. What came out at the meeting or what was meant to come out at the meeting was that I as the -- the head of the coordinating centre in Grude would take the agreed deliberations of all sides at this particular meeting, take with them with me to Gornji Vakuf and implement them on the ground. So the priority, the purpose of the meeting was to diffuse the situation in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you again if you remember this as you sit here today, I asked you already your observations, your recollection as to the relative position as between Mr. Prlic and Petkovic. Is that something that you remember to this day?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: My comments on the -- the question you've asked me would be based on my experience of these people throughout my stay there as opposed to just one meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And well, let's just continue with that then. Based on your experience throughout these months that you spent interacting with Mr. Prlic and Mr. Petkovic, can you tell us your view in terms of the respective positions of authority and decision-making?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, I think I already have. I said that it appeared to me that Mr. Prlic was the most influential person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at the bottom of page 1, just to come back to what you said there is a reference to ECMM head of Grude called to monitor delivery of the order. Is that a reference to you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That was my purpose at being at that meeting was to bring that order with me to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, if you would turn the page, please. And I want to direct you to item --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, the document was admitted on the 15th of May, 2006, through Witness Beese. So this is a document that has already been admitted into evidence. So the content is familiar to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and that's why -- and sincerely I'm just trying to pull out of the document those parts of it that relate to the witness's own story and evidence, and I just have a couple more points on this that I'd like to take him to with your permission. But I don't intend to go through this document in detail. But the witness was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And on that I would just like to ask the witness if he recalls, as reflected in item C, there is a reference to a decision. "Mr. Prlic said the HVO would not do anything to enact by force the decision sent to the BiH units." Do you recall what that decision was about? Do you know what that's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether -- well, let me direct your attention to Exhibit P 01155.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this one's already in evidence as well. I'm not going to go into it in great detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 1155. It's toward the beginning, I think, of the binder.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's a decision relating to subordination of units in different places. It's over the signature of Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I'd like some foundation. Did the gentleman see it? If he hasn't seen it, I would object on the grounds stated by Mr. Scott last week. We attempted to do this last week there were lots of suggestions by Mr. Scott that this is an improper technique. I draw the Court's attention that when the Prosecution does it, it seems to be okay, when the Defence does it the Prosecution objects. So in keeping with the Prosecution's own procedure, unless the gentleman saw this decision, is familiar with this decision then he cannot discuss the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question, Mr. President. Maybe we'll see what the witness can do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, I don't know how to respond to objections in advance of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He hasn't seen the document, but on the other hand, perhaps he's familiar with the contents of the document. So before showing him the document, ask him the question regarding the contents, because here we see certain regions mentioned and this may remind him of something. And before going into the details, perhaps one should start with the more general issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, based on your conversations with the HVO people that you've mentioned, the situation in Gornji Vakuf, did you have any awareness at the time of any linkage between events in Gornji Vakuf and issues involving subordination within cantons under Vance-Owen?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was aware of concerns with people in relation to subordination. I had -- I had -- this document you refer to I had not seen, but I was aware of the increase of tension on the ground. And just to repeat, my function out there was on the ground. So I was witnessing this tension increasing on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So was tension then linked to an issue involving this issue of subordination?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: There was -- there was grave concern with -- with the Muslim side in relation to -- to potential subordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the end of Mr. Bousseau's report he's recounting some statements made by Mr. Pasalic, but there's a reference to units and equipment of the Croatian army, the HV, and I wanted to ask you whether you observed or encountered Croatian army units or equipment during the course of your tour in the region.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah, on a number of occasions, only in Mostar. We observed some Croatian army vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the end of this there's also a reference to humanitarian aid convoys being blocked, and I wanted to ask you whether humanitarian aid convoys were an issue on your -- in your remit and whether you raised any issues like that with the HVO people.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: There -- there was an ongoing problem with the transport of humanitarian aid where vehicles were being stopped and turned back or just generally being held there for inordinate lengths of time. This was an ongoing problem which I would deal with on an ongoing basis. That's the reason Bousseau raised it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you to turn to Exhibit P 1238. In this -- in this earlier report of Mr. Bousseau that we were just looking at, you indicated that you were the ECMM person who was to deliver an order on the cease-fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recognise Exhibit number 1238?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: This was the -- the agreement that was drawn up, the order for the -- for the -- that I was to bring with me to Gornji Vakuf that all sides were meant to act on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this order was the result of the meeting held on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, then, what you did in order to carry out your function in taking this order and working to put it into effect?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I think time moved on in that Mr. Bousseau came to Gornji Vakuf himself with -- with General Petkovic and Pasalic and briefed -- and discussed with the local commanders the -- the application of this order on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Just maybe to set the time frame given. This document is dated the 20th of January.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Was it the 21st? It was very soon after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So we have the meeting with the Mr. Prlic, Petkovic, and Pasalic on the 19th; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That's right, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the 20th is the date that this order results. And then you're saying very soon after that then the order was --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. Was -- was brought up by Mr. Bousseau and the other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you return to Gornji Vakuf --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- with Mr. Bousseau at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And with Messrs. Pasalic and Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. We escorted them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How is that transportation up to Gornji Vakuf carried out?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, they came in their own vehicles, in the convoy with the ECMM vehicles, if I remember, and we drove -- we -- in fact, it was quite interesting. When we were stopped at a number of check-points once the people at the check-points recognised the seniority of the people in the vehicles in relation to Pasalic and Petkovic, the barriers lifted and we went straight through.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Based on what you saw, did General Petkovic have trouble getting through any HVO check-points?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. That's why I say it was a very smooth operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention now to Exhibit 1303. And do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is this a report again of Mr. Bousseau?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to -- well, just to continue on with the chronology then. In paragraph 1 Mr. Bousseau indicates that he chaired on the 21st --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- in BritBat Gornji Vakuf a meeting to establish the conditions of the cease-fire, et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this cease-fire is that the one that is --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- the agreement that we were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now do you recall: Did the cease-fire hold?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. No. No. The cease-fire -- it held for a short period of the time, but firing resumed then again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And it's indicated here then on the next day in the morning rounds of artillery from the HVO side began. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were present at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was your location? Were you at the UN --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: UNPROFOR headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, what you recall about the shelling that you saw on that day?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, it -- it was similar to the shelling we had seen before in that it was -- it was into the centre -- into the town of Gornji Vakuf. In fact, quite close again to the UNPROFOR headquarters. A significant amount of shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you have dealings yourself with Colonel Siljeg in respect of this cease-fire and the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Not at this particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. At what point did you begin having dealings with Colonel Siljeg?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Over the next number of weeks I attempted to reactivate the cease-fire, so with the -- with the approval of -- of Mr. Bousseau, we formed what had been listed back there as -- as a joint commission, and we tried to get all relevant parties to sit around a table to thrash out an effective cease-fire that would last. I ensured that the people who were at the table were in a position to negotiate for their different sides. In other words, one of the first questions I asked both sides at that -- that particular time was are you in a position to sign an agreed cease-fire deal? Both sides told me they were, so the negotiations continued, and continued for quite an extensive period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as those negotiations continued, did both sides support the -- the making and the implementation of a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The -- my experience in these deliberations, and we're talking about 12, 13 hours a day around a table, was that the Muslim side were clear in their objective, that they wished to get a cease-fire as soon as possible, and the -- the Croat side were very slow to agree to a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In this document, Mr. Bousseau indicates there's a political purpose close to ethnic cleansing that is linked to this operation in Gornji Vakuf, and I wanted to ask you whether at that point or at any point you shared that view?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: From a military perspective and remember I'm a military man, the action in Gornji Vakuf was a well-coordinated military -- well thought out military tactic. I would certainly -- from what I saw on the ground I would not argue with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to Exhibit -- well, let's me ask you this then I'll take you to the exhibit. Do you recall during this period of time, then, the issue of Muslims -- you say ethnic cleansing then. Was there an issue relating to Muslims who were displaced, those who became refugees as a result of this operation?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: We're kind of moving on a bit there. When -- when the cease-fire deal was agreed and signed off on, one very significant area that had to be dealt with was the number of people who had been moved from their homes and whose homes now were occupied by other people. The only comment I can make on that is it was something I was aware of, but it was also something, and again I'd like you just to see -- to -- to remember that I'm talking about working 16, 18 hours a day, seven days a week, trying to keep the tension in the area down so that we didn't get a return to what we had. So issues like that I put on the long finger. I tried to deal with other specific issues like humanitarian aid and issues like that, but I was aware of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. You said that you put those on the long finger. Maybe for the interpreters and the languages --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Sorry, yes. I beg your pardon. What I mean by that is that once we had a cease-fire in -- activated and effective, I had a number of other items on the agenda which I felt took precedence over what you just asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, on the second page of 1303 there's a reference to a meeting that Mr. Bousseau had with Mr. Prlic. It says: "I went this morning to Mostar." Do you see that? A private interview with Mr. Prlic. Now, this document is dated the 25th of January. My question is whether you were present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At any time did you -- well, Mr. Bousseau had returned to Mostar throughout this period, the long days. Were you then now staying, sleeping in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The -- the focus for ECMM had shifted now from Siroki Brijeg right up to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you were staying there then.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you to Exhibit P 1309. There's a reference in here -- well, before we do that, I apologise, let me just take you back to 1303, which is the document you were just looking at, second page. Do you know whether -- because you mentioned that, despite the cease-fire, HVO shelling began again on the 22nd. Do you know, did you ever hear in Gornji Vakuf about any additional orders that had gone out for the HVO and Siljeg to stop conducting military operations after the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. 1309. Paragraph 16 on the third page of four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go into that, you know, I see what my clever colleague is trying to do, but you have to go back to 1303 where it says: "Order was given," in paragraph 4. "Order was given." The gentleman just indicated that he was unaware of any order. Now we go to the next document and now here somebody else drafts that document where it says: "He had ordered." Obviously there is a disconnect. Now, I can cover this on cross, but I think in all fairness and in the interest of justice to Dr. Prlic this should be pointed out, and I see that my clever friend has conveniently skipped over that part after the gentleman indicated that he has no recollection of any order being given or being issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, again, I don't know what the objection is. Again, I think cross-examination is the time to raise most of what's been raised by counsel. I'm interested in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To see things clearly, Commandant, I'm going to focus on the situation. We have seen a whole series of documents. There is a document of the 15th of January, which indicates that -- that there's going to be the subordination of units. There are units of the BH army that are going under the control of the HVO, and HVO units that are now going to be subordinated to the BiH. And this document was signed by Mr. Prlic himself. Then there is the implementation of all this. The situation, according to the document that we have just reviewed, Gornji Vakuf appeared to be encircled by the HVO artillery, and in Gornji Vakuf there are the two factions, the HVO and the BiH. UNPROFOR and the European mission are endeavouring to achieve a generalise the cease-fire, and the last document, 1303, signed by Cikotic, Colonel Siljeg, Bousseau, Stewart, puts in place the dispositions, and I note that in paragraph F, as of February the 1st, the ABiH and HVO units which are not normally stationed in Gornji Vakuf must withdraw by February the 1st. All this appears to be functioning. Why is it not functioning? You who were present there, why was it not functioning when it would appear that at the highest political level there is the will to achieve a cease-fire. UNPROFOR and the European mission are signing a document, and nevertheless there is shooting that continues. In your opinion, why did this not function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's my opinion that the -- the -- the HVO commander of that particular area was not inclined to agree to a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we are. We come to the heart of the matter. You say that in your opinion the HVO commander for this region -- who was he then? Was it Colonel Blaskic or who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Siljeg. And why is he not obeying the military and political leadership of the HVO? Who would you interpret this, the fact that Colonel Siljeg is not obeying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's really a question I can't answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your view -- you can't answer it but, yes, in your opinion the person responsible would be Colonel Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the military commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we continue, just to clarify one point, Mr. President. It is our contention and we have heard evidence that the events in Gornji Vakuf occurred, or there was conflict before January 15th. My objection, and I wanted to draw this to the Court's attention, which is on -- based on these two documents is the one document where the gentleman did not attend the meeting it says "Order was given." Then he was being directed to another document, 1309, where there it says, "Prlic said he had ordered the HVO." Where the Prosecution is going is they're trying to demonstrate somehow that Mr. Prlic has command and control over the military, and what I wanted to point out to the Trial Chamber is that, first, the gentleman wasn't there at the meeting. Secondly, he wasn't aware of any order. Three, that the previous document which was conveniently skipped over by the Prosecution says order was given, not attributing it to Dr. Prlic. And then this other document that was not generated by Mr. Bousseau but by somebody else who summarised all these things, somehow ended up saying that Prlic said he had ordered, and that was my point. And since the gentleman was not present, he's unable to comment regarding that. I anticipated the line of questioning from the Prosecutor because I'm as prepared as he is and I know where he's going -- I think I know where he's going. And if I've erred he can skip over that part and move on to some other area of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, the point I wanted to make here was whether by this period of time, this document being the 25th, the earlier document was dated the 20 -- I'm sorry, this one, 1309, is the 26th I believe. I correct that. It's the 25th. As well as 1303. They're both dated the 25th of January. My question is whether by that point actually the -- the conflict had largely settled down, tension reduced, and was no longer as active or intense as it had been earlier.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. The area was quieter, no question about it, but it required a formal cease-fire agreement. Just on the question that's been raised here about the different -- the different orders. It's fair to say that there were a number of orders issued which were not acted on. In the end it was another order that was produced that was signed by all the different parties involved to bring the cease-fire to Gornji Vakuf. None of those -- and again I just want to refer to the point, that as the person on the ground putting in the 16, 18 hours a day, these orders were really -- they weren't working, and they really weren't relevant. So when we got the joint commission together with the relevant people authorised to sign on the dotted line, that's when we finalised the correct cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just to finish this one off because it's -- it's been raised or it's been anticipated where I'm going, and so let me just put the question to you directly. Based on your observations and your meetings, again with Mr. Prlic, Petkovic, did Mr. Prlic exercise command and control over the HVO military?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I said from the outset that I could never see a distinction between the -- the military side and the political side. To me it was just one mix. I said that from the very beginning, and that was my experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he ever indicate to you that he did not exercise control over --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The question is unfair. Did he ever ask him. That's the real question, because -- simply because I don't go around saying what I cannot do doesn't mean that I am doing it or incapable of doing it. The -- was the question asked do you exercise effective command and control? That's the question. And then if there was an answer, yes or no, we can proceed.
