utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, counsel's free to answer -- ask any question he likes on cross-examination. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think the question is unfair.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I promise I won't object when he does ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, the question is unfair and the gentleman knows that. In what context?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commandant, we've seen the entire process, and apparently didn't function, obviously it didn't function. When you would meet Mr. Bousseau at UNPROFOR with members of the international community, as a member of the military you would assess the situation. As a professional you must have assessed the situation, and you must have asked yourself why things were not functioning, and at that point in time Mr. Bousseau or someone else must have referred to the chain of command. Did you have any meetings in order to identify the problems, in order to find out why Colonel Siljeg wasn't obeying? Did you ever have such briefings or debriefings amongst yourselves in order to determine who in fact exercised power, whether it be military or political power? Were any such meetings held in order to identify the problems. When a system doesn't function it is because there are certain objective reasons for that. So did you undertake such work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, to -- to answer that question and without boring you again, I just want to reiterate that that time in Gornji Vakuf was a time of great stress, long hours of work, and the objective being to bring a cease-fire there. I really didn't have the opportunity, as you've asked, to sit down with Mr. Bousseau or anybody and to reflect on the chain of command or who was issuing decisions for who. My job was to bring a cease-fire to that area so we could get people -- lives back to some sort of normality. I identified Colonel Siljeg part of the problem that we had to deal with and face up. But to answer your question directly, the answer is no, I did not have any meetings to discuss that subject that you asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when the Prosecution asks you whether Mr. Prlic had military responsibility, you can't answer that question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I -- what I said, Your Honour, was -- and this wasn't just based on Gornji Vakuf, it was based on my experience from my first days in Mostar up to Gornji Vakuf. It appeared to me that for whatever reason there was no distinction in the structure of the HVO between the political side and military side. It seemed to be one mix together. That was my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have our break now as it's 20 to 6.00. We will have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll resume the hearing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, before I start with the witness I should just do two things now because the witness is of the -- has the understanding that court tomorrow is in the afternoon and it's in the morning, and I thought I would just inform of witness because I misinformed him this weekend about tomorrow. So we start 9.00 sharp tomorrow morning, for your information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll wait for my room for the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the second point was that I need to ask -- I'm going to be tendering this map into evidence which the witness placed the circle on. It's not a pivotal document but I think it's necessary for the witness to sign the map in order for me to tender it into evidence. It's IC 693.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Do sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, just a couple of last questions on the Gornji Vakuf conflict. You indicated that at some point a cease-fire agreement was implemented with the agreement of both parties; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: To get to the end of this -- this saga, I pointed out that while we have a lot of documents here with cease-fire options in them, they didn't work. In the end, the joint commission, as I pointed out to you, sat, and I had both sides at the table, both sides in a position to sign off on what we agreed at the table. So after extensive negotiations, deliberations going on for days and for hours, we eventually had a document, a cease-fire document, which was -- was agreed by both sides of the table that it would be signed. When I asked the Croatian side, the HVO side, to sign the document, they informed me that they couldn't sign it because Colonel Siljeg would have to come and he'd sign it, having already stated that we didn't need his presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, do you -- can you tell us approximately what the period of time is on this? We know that late January --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: We're --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- was the time in which the --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: We're --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- the active conflict ended.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Middle February I would say. We -- eventually Colonel Siljeg arrived at the -- at our location and was not impressed with the document. So he -- he balled the document up in his hand and sent it over in my direction, and I was quite incensed because I felt it was an attack on the European Commission as opposed to me personally. I explain the hard work that we'd all put in in trying to draft a document which was agreed by both sides and that I really felt that what he had just done was unacceptable. So that ended that meeting, and the next day I became aware of the fact that Colonel Siljeg attended a meeting in Kiseljak outside Sarajevo with UNPROFOR. So I took myself over to that meeting, which was a very high-level meeting. I pointed out that we were on the verge of a peace deal in Gornji Vakuf, an historic peace deal really, and that I had more or less all sides agreed to this and Colonel Siljeg was the only problem. I left that meeting, and as I drove back to Gornji Vakuf my vehicles were passed by Colonel Siljeg and his staff, and on my return to UNPROFOR headquarters, to the joint commission office, I found Colonel Siljeg with maps, JNA maps, indicating the locations of both the HVO and Armija troops in the area, and he was issuing orders to all sides for the withdrawal of forces, the closing in of defensive positions, and the complete withdrawal of -- of all forces. Quite an impressive military response, I must say. As a military man standing there watching this happen it was very impressive because he was not only controlling his own people, he was controlling the Armija also and they were taking orders from him. So then we got the movement back of the forces, the filling in of the defensive positions, and then we knew after that then we could start doing some serious work in Gornji Vakuf in that we could now bring some sort of stability to the area knowing that all these external forces had been removed from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, there has been some discussion about the extent to which the HVO chain of command was functioning in respect of Colonel Siljeg, and so my question is do you know whether in all of your dealings with him whether he was acting pursuant to orders or was he acting on his own? Do you know what is responsibility for his conduct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I have to say as a military man, again, Colonel Siljeg impressed me as a military person. To answer your question bluntly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then in respect of the HVO operation militarily in Gornji Vakuf as you saw it during this period, did that appear to be an organised, planned operation?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The military assets available to the HVO in the area as I saw them being withdrawn and as I saw Siljeg's plan come to fruition were impressive.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What about -- I'm not talking about the withdrawal now so much as the lead-up, the preparation, the execution of the military operation in mid-January.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: As I said to you, Siljeg, he's a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My question was more about the HVO itself and the extent to which it performed or executed the military operation. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Effectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, after the cease-fire was ultimately agreed, the withdrawal began, you mentioned filling in or dismantling defensive --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- positions. That was part of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As the situation then improved were you in a position to go into the town of Gornji Vakuf and to acquaint yourself with the extent to which the damage and the effects of the shelling that you've talked about?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: When we had -- when Colonel Siljeg had completed the withdrawal of forces, he approached me and said that he had completed, as he said, his part of the deal, whereupon I invited him to come for a walk into central Gornji Vakuf to witness the town, and he refused that offer. I went in, and the damage to Gornji Vakuf was -- was substantial. But I just want to refer to what I have said before. The functioning of the joint commission at that point was crucial, because now we had withdrawal of the forces. The defensive and all the other stuff was removed. The focus and the energy now had to be done maintaining a level of calm in the area by providing the -- by providing all sides with what they required, which at that time was humanitarian aid and all the rest of it, and that's where the next phase of the joint commission put its energy into.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You've said that the damage in Gornji Vakuf was substantial. I wonder if you could just give us more details about the nature of the destruction, what types of structures, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It was normal dwelling houses, invariably with artillery round, destruction as in roofs blown off, walls knocked out, and what you normally see in a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Exhibit P 9137 in the binder. Just to sort of tie off the joint commission. Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Now, this photograph was taken some time after the -- the start of the joint commission's activities in that you can see on the left-hand side as you look at it the -- the Muslim representatives and the Croat on the right talking to each other. We started that joint commission where people wouldn't sit at the same table. So to reach that stage there was -- as I've said before, my function, my purpose in life in these missions is to try and assist people where required and that what you're looking at that gave me great personal pleasure from the point of view where we went from serious situation to that, where we actually got people to sit down and talk and try and improve the lives of the people in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is that you seated at the head of the table?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I -- I chaired -- I chaired -- for the number of weeks I chaired every meeting of the joint commission every day, every meeting for hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then there's another gentleman who is dressed in what appears to be the EC white?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mr. Beese. Chris Beese, and you can see the empty seat to my left shoulder, as you're looking at it. He would normally sit there as my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I know it's been a long time. Are you able to identify any of the other people who appear in this photo?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It has been an awful long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, I want to ask you now a couple of questions. I want to come back to some of your discussions and meetings with some of the HVO authorities, officials that you've -- that you've described already starting with Mr. Boban. The meetings that you had with him, are you able to recall whether he gave you any insights, any information about broader goals?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Boban invariably would speak about the -- the plight of his people, as in the Croatian people, and the fact that Europe, us, now that we were there, should be in a position to assist them in -- to improve their plight. To answer your question, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you then about Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your discussions with him about the objectives or the goals of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Again, it's important to state that I never saw a distinction between the military or the political side of the HVO. To me it was one homogenous unit led at the top with -- with -- and -- and I say it clearly from my experience out there, six months out there, what I'd seen in Gornji Vakuf and Prozor, what I'd -- what I'd observed myself with my own eyes and what I'd listened to, I had the distinct impression that the -- the objective of what was going on out there was to move that part of Bosnia or Herzegovina in a closer alignment with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Prlic ever indicate to you where the Muslims would fall in that equation?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall having a conversation with him about a map or a drawing?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. It was a drawing. I've said before it was a map. In fact, it was just a simple drawing of a circle with a line down through the middle, and on one side we had Muslims and on the other we had Croats, and as you said, the Muslims -- sorry, Croats and the Serbs, and the third party were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you to say that again so that the record's clear.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It wasn't a map. It was just a circle, which was obviously Bosnia-Herzegovina, I presume, with a line down through the centre of it, one side with Croat and the other side Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall in what context he made this drawing or circle?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I can't -- I cannot remember the meeting, when it was, but I can distinctly remember the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What do you remember about the meeting other than that? Can you recall anything specifically?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It was held in his office, which was -- I mean, the -- the office was a lovely office, and in contrast to what was happening outside. It seemed to stand away from what was happening outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you indicated the location of this officer yearly?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. I think it was the Rondo roundabout.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What part of Mostar was that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That was on the west side of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In your discussions with Mr. Prlic did he appear to be informed of the events that were taking place in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Again I repeat what I said. As a key leader, when I came across something which I felt had to be acted on, the key leaders had to be approached and they had to be aware of the situation because they could change things. What we're talking about is a very small area, a very, very small area. So every -- I mean, to my knowledge if people didn't know what was going on, I found that hard to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the question was did Mr. Prlic ever indicate he did not know what was going on?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Oh, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, again same question in respect of Mr. Stojic again. Did he appear to be informed or uninformed?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I repeat -- I repeat it again. The key leaders I refer to must have known what was going on. I would engage them in key leader engagements and brief them on what I had seen. Again I repeat, it's a small area. Everybody knew what was going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again the same question in respect of General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It would be the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he appear to be in a position to assert control over his subordinates?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he appear to have knowledge and awareness of the events that were taking place in the region?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: My answer is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You've been very expeditious. We have another 40 minutes, 45 minutes, who wants to start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we start, Mr. President, I was wondering where is this so-called drawing, and when was it that this was brought to the Prosecution's attention about the drawing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're asking me, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking the President to ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, as far as the sketch is concerned, did it arrive this weekend? What does the witness recall?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can tell Your Honour this: During the course of the weekend we were looking at the witness statement which makes reference to this story, although it indicates that this was a map, and in meeting with the witness this weekend he said no, it wasn't a map. It was more as you described a circle or a drawing that Mr. Prlic made. We're looking for the paragraph in the witness statement which makes that reference. What I can tell the Trial Chamber is that we informed the Defence by letter over the weekend of that change or correction, if you will, to the witness statement. So counsel was informed about it yesterday when we learned of the correction. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So, Mr. Karnavas, apparently in the written statement the witness said that it was a map, and this weekend he corrected himself and said it wasn't a map, a circle that had been drawn, and the Prosecution informed you of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I have to look at the statement again. And I'm looking at the comments made by -- I received on 14th, 14th of October, 2007. And maybe because I'm tired or something, but I don't seem to see anything where it talks about a drawing versus a map. Perhaps I could have some assistance from the Prosecution where it is that it states that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Which paragraph are you referring to? Which paragraph in the witness's written statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 47 of the witness's statement, Mr. President. The last sentence in paragraph 47. And as I indicated, we -- we informed counsel of the paragraph number in which the change was reflected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's paragraph 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, because given his testimony today, it seems rather different. And I don't see it in the correction, but again -- very well. Your Honour, I could begin now or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I might just follow up on your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, is -- do you have this map, this -- this sketch? That was Mr. Karnavas's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can begin now or we can start tomorrow. I believe it -- I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do start. Time is precious. We shouldn't waste it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lane. We haven't properly introduced ourselves. My name is Michael Karnavas. I represent Dr. Jadranko Prlic. You're going to have to speak up to make sure that we get a clear record. Now, if I listened to you correctly, as I understand you, before you set off to Bosnia-Herzegovina you received little, if any, instructions?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And while there was some sort of a briefing as far as what to expect, I take it, they did not give you any sort of a briefing as to the who's who?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when you -- when you -- now, you had been in -- in -- before going to Bosnia and Herzegovina you had been in some other area, as I understand it, for two or three weeks.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: In Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In Krajina. And -- and so -- and that was sort of a different mission?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, it was part of the ECM mandate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And as far as I understand it from your -- from your statement, all you did was drive around in the back of a car for that three-week period?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was only beginning my job if you like. Learning the ropes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So the answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So after that you went back to Split, or Zagreb, and that's where you got this briefing, such as it was, and then you -- you went to open up the office, as it were.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understand it, prior to go to country, to BiH, there was some sort of conflict between you and some other gentleman, the gentleman who in fact was giving you the briefing. You mentioned that in your statement.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So -- I may want -- I was not anticipating starting today, Your Honour, but I do have the documents that I might be referring to. Probably we'll get to them tomorrow, but we can share them with everyone today. There's not much, but anyway. All right. Now -- so this is -- and this gentleman was also working for the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And does he have a name?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Jeff -- Mr. Jeff Beaumont.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's British?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: He's British.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And had he been around longer than you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had he been in country or was he over there at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: He had -- he was in country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understand it the conflict was he had anticipated heading off -- starting the mission and instead somebody who was sort of a, for lack of a better word, a tenderfoot, somebody new --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Not that tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not that tender, but new to this particular region.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there was some friction?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: There was no friction. He was disappointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay but then he eventually he joined you in country?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also at one point I believe you said in your statement he had to be dismissed because I believe the word used was "clandestine", clandestine meetings with Mr. Siljeg or Colonel Siljeg?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was aware that he was having meetings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you used the word clandestine?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Without my approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Nothing --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The word "clandestine" probably isn't the right word in the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you were aware of those meetings or is it something that -- he was doing it on the sly?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the sly. Is that yes?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the sly?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was he not writing reports?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. I wasn't -- he was in Tomislavgrad. I was getting no reports from what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: And then he was meeting key leaders without the knowledge of the HCC. So in other words there was no coordination in the activity in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words what he was learning, if he was learning anything, wasn't being passed on to you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then you needed that because you needed to pass it up to --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Up the line?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right now let's briefly speak about when you got to Mostar. You already told us today how it is that you ended up setting up shop in Siroki Brijeg, but as I understand it, Mostar, as you put it, was the priority. Those are the words that you used?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I even took some notes today.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Good, yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you said one of the things you wanted to do was to seek out and meet and perhaps even develop some relationships with the key leaders in the community. Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes. I said that, yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't hear you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't mean to be pushy.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, no, no. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and it wasn't until you were there for about a week and a half that you ended up walking across the bridge to -- and meeting with the other side, as it were, you know, the Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: As I said to you, I'm not quite sure of the time scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But it was some time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It was some time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was enough time at least for Mr. Pasalic who obviously was keeping track of you, although, let's face it would not have been very difficult with your white ice cream sort of suit, you know -- you know, to be spotted so it was long enough at least for him to be rather, for lack of a better term, discontent with the fact that they were -- that side was being ignored?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was not your intention though?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and you said that had you known, had you known, had you -- in other words, if you had had a better briefing, you probably would have gone there earlier; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That's a fair comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause between question and answer for the interpreters, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it the folks in Zagreb or Split or wherever you got this briefing didn't even know the difference between the west side and the east side, who lived on one side, who lived on the other and what exactly was happening in Mostar. I mean, that's the impression I'm getting.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Or else I was briefed on it and I didn't pick it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. All right. Now, again I just want to make sure I'm clear in my mind because you're setting off, you're going into this area, you're going to set up shop, you've never been to this region for all intents and purposes in this sort of a mission; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: In -- in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In that area?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You've been to Lebanon and all these other places, fair enough, do they ever bother to give you some sort of a schematic, some sort of flow chart as far as what to expect on the political level, the structure itself? And that calls for a yes or no or I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Ask me the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Before setting -- while you were getting this briefing and before setting out, did those who briefed you give you some sort of a schematic, you know, of where the chain of command or where the powers lie?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, did they bother to give you a briefing, for instance - now we're going to go into a little more specific - into the personalities, such as who is Mate Boban, what his title is and what his de jure, his legal function and perhaps maybe even if he has some de facto function, you know, or powers. Did they give you that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did they do that for any of the other gentlemen that you were asked about such as Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Coric, General Petkovic, General Praljak, did they do that? Or would the answer be the same?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The answer is not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And if you could have remembered it at least when you gave the statement because there are some things in the statement that are rather specific you would have put that in; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: If I had -- say again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you had remembered it back then. If you can't remember it today --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- you didn't remember it back in 2004 when you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you gave that statement in 2004, incidentally - because I see it's Mr. Spork who is with the OTP who took the statement - did he show you any documents to sort of refresh your memory or walk you down memory lane as it were before giving the statement or did he just ask you a bunch of questions, tell me what you know --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and I'll write it down?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That was the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and I take it over the weekend when you were being briefed by the Prosecutor - I didn't mean to say "briefed" but let's say proofed - you had a copy of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's a yes?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You read it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You read it thoroughly?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They also showed you some documents?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and I take it some of those documents were shown to you in order to somewhat refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I don't know if that was the purpose of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, I didn't say it was but it did refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right, and did they show you documents which you were unaware of, documents that you had never seen. Maybe you knew the contents of the documents --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- but had never seen before?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Just to make a general point if I may I was out running this morning on the beach and as I'm running - because this is all coming back 15 years later - it's amazing what the mind opens up to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sort of a moment of clarity?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, just things you've forgotten about, buried, come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, okay, all right. Is there some revelation that happened on the beach?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Maybe you don't want them to come back?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, okay, all right. Now, when you got to -- when you got to Mostar, may I ask how is it that you knew who to see? Open-ended question?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Very simple answer to that: You will see that I mentioned that we hired an interpreter, an Australian interpreter called Judy Zvoko who had good knowledge of the key leaders in the area. So she briefed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and was she living on the east side or the west --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: West side, west side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and did you ask her, did you rely on her to tell you who was who?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Her -- yeah. Her initially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: In the beginning, yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right and I'm asking that question because today it seemed that you were struggling somewhat, albeit you gave a statement, as to what exact function Mr. Stojic had. And you know and I'm saying this and I'm not trying to --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not trying to --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- embarrass you but you said that you met him on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You know you have vivid memories at least back in 2004 with certain things and yet when asked what function this individual had that you met --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- almost on a weekly basis you were unable to tell us.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, there are two aspects to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Two aspects to what?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: To your question. And just let me let me deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: One is, as I've said throughout my few words today, we're 15 years later, and lot of water has flowed under the river since then, and secondly, being a soldier as I am, and I've said it umpteen times today --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right, right.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: -- My priority is to identify problems in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: And put my energy in there to resolve those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: So let me finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go for it. Go for it.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: So when there's people sitting around a table who can help me, key leaders as I've said, that's what I'm there for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Finished?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Fair enough, I heard that. You've said it many times. You have to know - would you agree with me? - who the key leaders are. Number one, right? That's a starting point?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel I'm sorry for the interruption but at line 16 we didn't get in the transcript the witness's complete answer to that question and I wonder if we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's been recorded, Your Honour, it's been recorded but if -- it's -- we have a recording, they can catch it, but I don't have any objections to it being -- for the complete answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Maybe if the witness could just say his answer again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so you said when there's people sitting around a table to help, do you recall what you said after but we do have a recording. We have an excellent, excellent stenographer although I'm speaking too fast. That is the problem. And you are too sir.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I'll -- I'll slow down. Yes. What I was actually going to say there was and I've said it also a lot today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I'm talking about a homogenous group of people. I never saw a line down the middle between political and military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I finished this since you asked the question. So these people, as far as I'm concerned, whatever problem I would bring to that table had the know all and the wherewithal to solve those problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, now, let's go back to what I was asking. You said that you wanted to know who the key leaders were and I'm asking, first of all, you need to find out who they are; right? You're shaking your head, that means yes?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Sorry. Absolutely yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and then I would assume you would want to know what their function is, their individual function. I know you're a military man but you want to know exactly who can do what. We're going to the general questions and then we'll go to the specifics?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that's the next step. You want to find out if this is a key leader, what exactly is his title and what his functions are?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Let me ask you this: What efforts, if any, did you make to find out how the political system was structured? In other words, who held what title, what were the positions, how were decisions made, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What efforts? Just work with me on that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I'm sure. As part of the process of briefing my monitors and going about their daily work, as I've said to you, part of their function was to go and visit these leaders and to draw up a structure that we thought was there at the time. More specific than that I cannot be because I can't actually remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Lane, you're -- you're the head honcho. You're the number one, the big cheese?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, not a big cheese, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Over there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. Small cheese.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you were the head of the mission right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For your team, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was the head of the team. I was head of the coordination centre, not the head of the mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, not the head of the whole mission, but you were head of the team; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The head of the coordination centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I had a number of teams working for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so people were coming up to you.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm asking you concretely --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- did you ever make any efforts to find out who held what position and how was the political structure functioning? And it's a yes, no, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel, I'm just again looking at line 2 at page 116. Again, I think it may be because of the speed that the question and answer is happening but we missed again the witness's answer to counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll slow down to avoid the interruptions, Your Honour. Although Mr. Stringer, being a veteran of this institution knows that everything is being transcribed but I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, it's not being transcribed, that's the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's being recorded, he understands that. And before we have a final transcript they go over it. But I understand the technique. I understand the technique of interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So do you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Touche.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Lane, going back, could you describe to us exactly what -- what function Mr. Prlic had? I don't want to hear the same old --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- well, they're all blending. I'm asking you concretely, specifically: Do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I answered you already. As far as I -- I was concerned, Mr. Prlic was the head honcho as you described.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: He was the boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now let me ask you this: How -- based on what documentation, based on what -- did you look at did you look at any documents to see how, any Official Gazettes, anything? Did you get a briefing?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. I think in fact more importantly I got it from on the ground which I keep referring to today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay and who was on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, but you're getting it on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Driving around, interviewing people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Talking to people, getting my teams reporting back to me. That's what I mean by "on the ground".

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you not also said that Mr. Boban was the number one?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, you asked me about Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now I'm asking you: Have you not also said that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Quite clearly what I was asked today, and I repeat what I said, when I was asked to put them in sequence I put Mr. Boban number one and then Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: But you asked me about Mr. Prlic there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now you said "on the ground." Let me ask you this since you were getting all your information on the ground --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It took a week and a half to go over the bridge to figure out that that's where the Muslims were. That's the interpretation I got.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: What I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me finish my question please?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My question is this: Where were the headquarters of the ABiH? Which side? Because you're getting your information on the ground. So from the ground, tell me where were the headquarters of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: West Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: West Mostar, not East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, West.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, how is it that you visit the east side to see Mr. Pasalic if you know that the headquarters are on the west side?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The reason I visited the east side was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, just answer my question: How is it that you don't go - you're a military man - how is it you don't go to the west side to their headquarters to meet with them and then you decide to meet Mr. Pasalic on the east side?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I don't know. Can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the headquarters on the west side?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who did you meet there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You mean it was a low-level --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- soldier?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was it Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I just said I can't remember. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How is it that when it comes to the Croats, you remember, when it comes to the Muslims you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It's 15 years on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's my point.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: 15 years on, significant things hopefully stick in your mind and other things don't. That's the point I'm making to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, now, you say that Mr. Prlic's office was on the Rondo. Would it surprise you, sir, to learn that his office was in Hotel Ero?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Well, the office I met him in was on the Rondo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what you -- and you assume that was his office?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That's where I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You met him -- every time you met him there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Maybe not, but a lot of the time I met him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever met him in Hotel Ero?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down for the interpreters, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that a yes or no or I don't know?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicate -- now, you gave a statement and I notice that this wasn't touched upon, but in your statement you said that Mr. Prlic had a private restaurant.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That could be the hotel you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, but not -- I thought you said his office was in the Rondo now you're talking about he had about a hotel.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, I'll be very -- I'll be clear on what I'm saying I said I went to his office on the Rondo. You referred to the hotel. I said I wasn't sure but perhaps I was there, and in the restaurant that's your -- that's your reading but that possibly was the hotel, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you visited him at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, I said that I said that it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But in your statement in 2004 you seem to be rather clear and I look at the pages and they all seem to have your initial because obviously you read them, you read the statement, right? And this is because today I see that you've made numerous corrections, all right? Now, there you say that he had a private restaurant. Now, did you have the discussion with the Prosecutor regarding this private restaurant in the briefing session today?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Did I have a what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did this come up during the proofing session?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: The location of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, the -- because you -- it wasn't mentioned. I mean, this is something that the Prosecutor would have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So did this come up during the proofing session?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: It was part of what I read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, when you were proofed by the Prosecutor, when he was preparing you to go through certain documents, did he mention, did he ask you any questions with respect to this private restaurant that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. What he asked me was specifically to locate the office that I had visited Mr. Prlic in, which I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: On the Rondo. But I also mentioned about the restaurant and I couldn't remember where this restaurant was but you have now mentioned the hotel and it's a possibility that that's where I met Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, and my question now is: Did this conversation come up during the proofing session with this particular gentleman?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's been asked and answered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So the answer is, no, it didn't come up?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's on the record. It's been asked and answered. He's given his response.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did the gentleman there ask you about the private restaurant that you make references to? Yes or no? This is the gentleman we're talking about. We're not talking about the other investigator that wrote this report. We're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm looking at line 15 of page 121, asking whether it came up during the proofing session, and continuing down: "What he asked me specifically to locate the office that I had visited Mr. Prlic in." I think the witness has given his response to this question about the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the restaurant is separate from the office. Now, Mr. Stringer may wish to testify and tell us, did he ask him the question about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you asked by this gentleman about this -- this so-called private restaurant, because you made representations to the Prosecutor back in 2004 that there was some sort of a private restaurant that Mr. Prlic had with the waiter coming and all of that.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did this come up during your proofing session with Mr. Stringer, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Specifically that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's it. Fair enough. Now, when you gave this statement, you were under the impression that Mr. Prlic had a private restaurant. You're shaking your head, nodding it. Does that mean yes?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I wrote, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever -- was that something that you got from the ground?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the private restaurant, whether you say private restaurant, in your mind, in the army a high-ranking general may have a place where he receives his guests of some standing. When you saw Mr. Prlic, perhaps you meant to say that Mr. Prlic may be receiving persons in a particular restaurant in a private or official capacity, or was Mr. Prlic a restaurant owner? There's some confusion there. Could you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm missing the point here, but what I said was I met Mr. Prlic in a facility that appeared to be a dining facility, an up-market dining facility. What I said was I wasn't aware where it was but when -- when the Defence then mentioned the hotel, then obviously that became a possibility that's where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. May I continue? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The reason I'm pushing you is because in 2004 you gave certain impressions to the Prosecutor. Those impressions were based on your memory.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They were also based on the information you were collecting from the ground and from your observations. You said you were there six months. Now, in paragraph 57, for instance, you say: "It should be noted that Mr. Prlic private restaurant was on the top of a building overlooking East Mostar." And then you go on. Now, today, as you sit here today, after your little jog on the Scheveningen beach, okay? Because I don't know what came back, you know, as you were sort of thinking back 15 years ago, do you still maintain that Mr. Prlic had a private restaurant, because that what -- that is what you represented to the Office of the Prosecution when they came to you and they were asking you for concrete information.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. To the best -- to the best of my knowledge, what I said at the time actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not saying what happened. You represented that he had a private restaurant.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I want to know concretely, sir --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- is that your position today?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would it surprise you, sir, to learn that the food that was being delivered as was alluded to by the President, came from the restaurant downstairs from Hotel Ero, that that was the hotel restaurant and not Mr. Prlic's restaurant? Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, not in the least, because when you mentioned the hotel's name I said to you there was a possibility that's where I met him, so to answer your question does it surprise me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You met him -- when you would have -- when he invited you as a guest to have conversations and you would have -- share a meal, it was -- it was a room; right? Not in a regular restaurant. It was a private room; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Somebody would come in wearing a bow tie or whatever, however waiters dress?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes? That's a --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And they would give you the food?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you would sit there and you would have discussions with Mr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Excuse me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understand it from speaking with Mr. Prlic, he made himself available to you. Whenever you wanted to see him, he was there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I said that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You said that in your statement and you're saying that today?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Here, however, when you gave your statement to the Prosecutor, and an objective reader, reading what you stated, walks away with the impression that you, six months on the ground, and getting your information from the ground, were of the opinion that Mr. Prlic had a private restaurant and that he was privately being served, when in fact it appears that you're meeting him in the Hotel Ero where he had his office on the fourth or fifth floor and the food was being delivered from the hotel restaurant. Now, given that, assuming that's correct and we'll bring in evidence to prove all of this, would you not say that you're on the ground knowledge and observation, at least on this particular issue, is way off?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you maintain that he still had a private restaurant?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I maintain my choice of words might be -- might have been better if I'd remembered correctly what happened that particular day or those days, but the essence of what I said still stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The essence still stands.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. It was a restaurant. It was private. The food was served privately to myself and Mr. Prlic by waiter service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that when you gave this statement and reading this statement is it doesn't give that impression. Rather, you're trying to give the impression that Mr. Prlic had a private restaurant.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With private dining facilities. Okay. Very well. Now, did you ever ask Mr. Prlic in all these meetings for him to specify exactly to you what his functions were, what he could and could not do? I'm going to ask the question that the Prosecutor didn't ask you. Did you ever sit down and ask him concretely: Tell me what are your functions?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What do you mean you cannot remember?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I -- I can't rather if I did or didn't ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you had asked him that and had you had that information, don't you think that that's the sort of information that you would have shared with the folks that you had to report to?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I go back to what I said earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, let me ask you -- please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you -- if you -- if you had asked that question and if you had received information, concrete information, from one of the key persons of what his functions were and what his -- and what he was capable of doing, would you not have put that into a report, done some sort of briefing and passed it up the chain of command; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: No. What I actually said to you was I can't remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you whether you can remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking is that the sort of information you would put in a report --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have limited time, Your Honour, and the gentleman is -- I know it's late in the day but I'm asking very specific questions. Let me slow it down, let me slow it down, okay? I'm going to take a deep breath now.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: You need a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask it again, okay? Just the last question and then we can break for the day, because I'm going to switch to other topics. If you had in any of your meetings with Mr. Prlic or anybody else for that matter --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- a conversation, a meeting, and if during that meeting you had asked the gentleman concretely what his functions were, de facto, de jure, what he could or could not do, is that the sort of information that you would have put down and passed it up the chain so that at least everybody would know what exactly you were learning?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So when you say you don't remember, if that -- that indeed had occurred with you at least, Mr. Lane, we would have some sort of document where you sit down and say at this meeting I asked concretely Mr. Prlic to explain to me who is doing what, what his functions are, what he's capable of doing. We would have some sort of document. Please answer my --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Absolutely, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, all right, that's all I wanted. You want to say something?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Supplement it.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: That is not to say that that wasn't done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE
utterances.text: Yeah. In fact, there probably are documents there in the RC with that kind of information on it.
